citations.quote: Portfolio A is overpriced relative to portfolio C. An arbitrageur can short the securities in portfolio A and buy the securities in portfolio C
Put–call parity is a relationship between the price, c, of a European call option on a stock and the price, p, of a European put option on a stock
Comparing Exhibit 13 with Exhibit 14 shows that a protective put and a fiduciary call produce the same result
Put–call parity does not tell us which price is correct, and it requires knowledge of one price to get the other

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: European put-call parity is the model-free no-arbitrage identity C - P = S0 - K·exp(-rT) linking call, put, spot, and risk-free bond. The proof is a portfolio dominance argument: a long call plus a bond paying K replicates a long put plus the underlying at expiry (both pay max(ST,K)), forcing equal initial cost.
